articles.excerpt: Visualiser une protéine en VR change-t-il vraiment quelque chose pour ceux qui l'enseignent ? Quand une annonce comme « Gemini 4 Carbon » promet d'accélérer la science, je suis partagé. Sur le fond, l…
articles.body: Visualiser une protéine en VR change-t-il vraiment quelque chose pour ceux qui l'enseignent ? Quand une annonce comme « Gemini 4 Carbon » promet d'accélérer la science, je suis partagé. Sur le fond, les modèles de repliement ont transformé le travail de beaucoup d'entre nous. Mais il reste un point que ces annonces sous-estiment : le temps qu'un humain met à comprendre une structure. Un fichier PDB prédit en quelques minutes ne devient pas une intuition pour autant. J'ai passé des années devant des rendus 2D sur écran plat avant de vraiment « sentir » une poche de liaison. C'est ce décalage que j'explore aujourd'hui avec NexoPeek, un laboratoire moléculaire VR sur Meta Quest. Pour être clair sur le positionnement : ce n'est ni un substitut à PyMOL ou ChimeraX, ni un pipeline validé.

articles.title: How to Choose 3 Healthtech Email API Paths: Retention Rules That Survive Audits
articles.excerpt: Short answer: choose the email API whose evidence, retry behavior, and deletion controls explain one welcome message from contact form to support queue without retaining more health data than the work…
articles.body: Short answer: choose the email API whose evidence, retry behavior, and deletion controls explain one welcome message from contact form to support queue without retaining more health data than the workflow needs. Personalization is a constrained data projection. It is not permission to copy the entire request into an email. That boundary matters. Start with the retention bill, not the send button The bill is made of retained records, delivery events, rendered content, attachments, logs, and retries. For this workflow, the dominant term is usually event history: one accepted message can create several transitions, and a long retention window multiplies them. Measure submissions per day, events per submission, bytes per event, and retention days before comparing APIs.

articles.title: Forward Watch
articles.excerpt: AI Object Detection for Recreational Boats Every skipper knows the moment: a log just under the surface, a kayak hidden in sun glare, or a small boat with no AIS crossing ahead at dusk. Keeping a prop…
articles.body: AI Object Detection for Recreational Boats Every skipper knows the moment: a log just under the surface, a kayak hidden in sun glare, or a small boat with no AIS crossing ahead at dusk. Keeping a proper lookout is a legal and practical duty, but human eyes get tired. Forward Watch is an AI-powered assistant to that lookout. It is an open-source Signal K plugin , published on npm as signalk-forward-watch, and it's part of the d3kOS platform. The Problem Many of the hazards that matter most to recreational boaters are invisible to electronics: Debris and logs don't transmit anything. Kayaks, paddleboards and small boats usually have no AIS. Buoys are on the chart, but not always where you expect in poor visibility. Radar may not be fitted, and small or low targets can be hard to pick out.

articles.title: Surviving AWS Spot Interruptions With Real Checkpointing
articles.excerpt: 🔧 The Problem Spot instances are 60-90% cheaper than on-demand, and the pitch is always the same: "just make your workload fault-tolerant." Great, thanks. In practice, most teams discover their batch…
articles.body: 🔧 The Problem Spot instances are 60-90% cheaper than on-demand, and the pitch is always the same: "just make your workload fault-tolerant." Great, thanks. In practice, most teams discover their batch job, training run, or queue worker isn't actually fault-tolerant until the first 3am page from a spot reclamation mid-run. The naive fix is restarting the job from scratch after interruption. For a 20-minute job, fine. For an 8-hour fine-tuning run or a multi-hour ETL batch, restarting from zero isn't resilience, it's just burning compute budget until you get lucky with instance availability. This post is about the pattern that actually makes spot interruptions a non-event: a tight interruption handler plus a checkpoint cadence tuned to your workload's actual cost of re-doing work.

articles.title: Same model, same defences: 7 document attacks down to 0, chat attacks barely moved
articles.excerpt: A prompt-injection benchmark, three bugs in my own scorer, and the result I only found after fixing them. I built RAGProbe, an open-source tool that throws prompt-injection attacks at LLM apps and mea…
articles.body: A prompt-injection benchmark, three bugs in my own scorer, and the result I only found after fixing them. I built RAGProbe, an open-source tool that throws prompt-injection attacks at LLM apps and measures what lands. I published the numbers. Then I pointed a fresh AI session at the repo, gave it no context, told it to be brutal, and checked everything it found. It found three real bugs in my code and one claim that was wrong. Mildly humbling for a project whose entire pitch is "scoring you can check". The re-run gave me a better result than the one I'd announced, so here's what happened. Scoring an attack without asking another model Many injection evaluations end the same way: a second LLM reads the reply and decides whether the attack worked.

articles.excerpt: The numbers look impressive, but the threats haven't vanished.
articles.body: TL;DR T-Mobile says successful SIM swap attacks have dropped by more than 99% since 2022, following stronger account security measures. The carrier also reports a 99% reduction in phishing-related employee credential compromises and billions of blocked scam calls and texts. Despite these improvements, attempted intrusions increased 37% over a recent 12-month period, showing that security threats remain a serious challenge. T-Mobile knows better than most carriers how expensive a stolen phone number can become. Early last year, the Un-carrier paid out $33 million after a SIM swap attack cost a customer $38 million in cryptocurrency. Add the carrier’s troubled history with data breaches , and it’s easy to see why security promises alone might not inspire much confidence.

articles.title: James Webb Space Telescope uncovers new clues about the origins of 'interstellar invader' comet 3I/ATLAS
articles.excerpt: The findings are another clue towards understanding the origins of 3I/ATLAS and the planet-forming conditions around other stars.
articles.body: Using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), scientists have found that the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS was built from tiny grains of ice mixed with dust that are quite different from the solar system’s comets. These ice grains do, however, bear striking similarities to some icy bodies located at the edge of the solar system, beyond the orbit of Neptune, so-called trans-Neptunian objects (TNOs). 3I/ATLAS was discovered entering the solar system in the summer of 2025. It was only the third object found entering the solar system from farther afield in the Milky Way after 1I/'Oumuamua , seen in 2017, and 2I/Borisov , detected in 2019. This meant the interstellar comet offered a rare chance to glimpse the conditions under which such bodies form in other star systems.

articles.title: Raising the quality of insights in agentic analytics
articles.excerpt: In just a few years, generative AI has changed the face of enterprise analytics, notably by making analytics accessible to users across the organization. Agentic AI promises to do even more, by automa…
articles.body: In just a few years, generative AI has changed the face of enterprise analytics, notably by making analytics accessible to users across the organization. Agentic AI promises to do even more, by automating entire workflows and taking actions based on agent insights. But there is a problem: The quality of insights that agents currently generate leaves much to be desired. Fewer than half of agent-generated insights at the organizations surveyed for this report lead to business improvement. And while most respondents praise the quality of their agents’ descriptive insights, reviews of their prescriptive insights—those on which actions are based—are decidedly mixed.
